payload.title: install replaces a host's own ~/.cratylus.json and uninstall then deletes it
payload.body: Beside the assay of install of guided-install at d65e7db7, observed in live temp-HOME runs. A ~/.cratylus.json the host wrote before any install ({"x":1}, or {"configuration":{"mine":{"a":1}}}) is replaced by install: its keys are gone afterwards, and neither the preview nor the summary names the file. uninstall of the only harness then removes the whole file as 'the runtime config: claude was its last harness', so the host's content is lost for good. A host edit made after install is handled (uninstall takes out only the harness stanza and keeps the file), and two harnesses sharing the file are handled. Whether a pre-existing file at that path is the host's to keep, or cratylus's by its name, is the runtime config concept's question; it lies outside install's closure, so it was not counted in that verdict.
